note: The transfer and trial of the two suspects under resolution 1192 are the handling of the Lockerbie bombing, an act on the Council's closed list (4.6).
ASEAN's support for a long-term solution to restore stability in Myanmar, after the extremist violence and overreaction described, concerns a specific identifiable crisis (4.10).
The clause 'many of them are gang-related' has the gangs as perpetrators of the murders for its whole claim (5.2 row (e)).
Reform of the judiciary's independence is paired with the anti-corruption office as the object of the sentence, and measures on public security follow (3.2, 4.9, section 8).

The Athens, Lod and Munich attacks appear only in relative, time and pretext clauses of sentences about Israeli raids, and alleged transit through Lebanon is no accusation of State support (3.2, 4.6).

Collective security is invoked as the Organization's founding purpose with no conflict, Council reform or measure, and peace otherwise appears in an enumeration of the Organization's capacities (4.10).
Counter-terrorism cooperation is one verb-phrase item in a series of the Forum's measures, with no fact or measure of its own (3.2).
Two sentences are about the Geneva Conventions and the protection of civilians in war, a peace-and-security matter (YAML include) rather than a general invocation (4.10).
Boko Haram is on the Council's closed list and counts without the word, but its abduction of girls is one example in an enumeration (4.6, 3.2).
Peacekeepers appear only in an inclusion phrase and relative clause of a sentence crediting UN staff, and in thanks; 'these successes' refers outside the fragment (3.2).
The Munich agreement and appeasement of the Third Reich are the object of the sentence and characterized as a lesson, not only a date (3.2, 4.10).
'The country of gangs' is one of two examples of the country's former reputation and is not developed (3.2).
The last sentence is about taking hundreds of civilians as hostages and the fragment does not place it in the inter-State war of the previous sentence (5.2 row (a)).
The Iran deal, the nuclear agreement, is the subject of two sentences, and arms control is peace however framed (4.10).
The Hamas attack, called a terror attack, is named within the object of the condemnation, a single inclusion rather than an enumeration (3.2, 4.6).
The struggle against terrorism and conflict settlement are requirements in a series across sentences sharing the subject 'security', neither developed (3.2).
Drone deals and security agreements are arms transfers and defence cooperation between States, which 4.4 and 5.1 assign to peace.
Security Council reform is included in the subject of the claim that reform is imperative, a single inclusion rather than an enumeration (3.2, 4.10).
'This type of crime' and the acts to be repressed are the terrorism, kidnapping and hijacking discussed, so enforcement against them adds no criminal_justice (4.9).
The MMS and a strong force with a clear mandate for Haiti are the missions that 4.10 assigns to peace even for gang violence.
Interference, subversion and infiltration by unnamed Powers and agent States are described in general, with no identifiable conflict, parties or act (4.10).
The threat of nuclear war poisoning international relations is the claim of its own sentence, the nuclear danger that counts without a named conflict (3.2, 4.10).
The response to the rise in crime gives authority to the high courts, which are ready to hear any case of violation of the law, an item developed with a fact of its own (3.2, 4.9).
Support for the call to halt the illegal trade in small arms makes the illicit trade the object of the claim, organized_crime whoever receives the arms (4.4).
The claim that named regions are safer without Mullah Omar, Saddam Hussein and Milosevic concerns identifiable parties and places of conflict (4.10).
Cuba's designation as a sponsor of terrorism, rejected in a clause about the blockade, is a national listing with no discussion of terrorism itself (4.6).
The first sentence is about the destructiveness of the Second World War, a named war, not only a date or the founding narrative (4.10).
Cologne flattened by bombing in 1947 identifies a specific war by place and act, and the sentences describe what that war did to the city (4.10).
Organized crime is one item of a series of commitments with the justice system and corruption, and the later sentences develop only corruption (state capture, stolen money) (3.2).
The consequence clause, excluded young people falling prey to organized crime and terrorism, carries the point taken up by the next sentence and gives both a cause (3.2).
The Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice is one of the two bodies whose merger is the object of concern, and its criminal focus is the reason for it (3.2, 4.9).
International terrorism is one item of a series and Islamic terrorism one of two things the UN is said to ignore, neither developed (3.2).

The demand that Hamas release Israeli hostages is not framed as a ceasefire term and the next sentence condemns using civilians as pawns, so hostage-holding outside a war between States counts (5.2 row (a)).
Ending war propaganda that poisons international relations and promoting contacts between organizations of differing outlooks are measures against tension between the blocs (4.10).
Terrorism is one of three customary companions of regional conflicts named in an enumeration, with no claim of its own (3.2).
'The bloodshed' that threatens a new world conflagration is not identified by parties, place or act, and the rest invokes peace as an aim (3.2, 4.10).
The convention for judicial cooperation on felonies is cooperation in criminal matters with no single crime named, and no criminal group is named (4.9, 5.1).
Attacks on humanitarian personnel and journalists are condemned with no war, conflict or peace measure mentioned (4.10).
'International criminal activity' appears only in a participial clause giving the reason for the drug and money-laundering policy, and international crime is not crime in general (3.2, 5.2).
Curbing the illicit trade in small arms is one of the two paired aims of the treaty, organized_crime whoever receives the arms (3.2, 4.4).
Crime is one item of an agenda enumeration (5.2); the Crime Prevention Centre appears only as secretariat of the organized crime convention.
Support for an instrument to check the illegal trade in small arms makes the illicit trade the object of the claim, organized_crime whoever receives the arms (4.4).
Defeating terrorism and fighting transnational crime are the two paired purposes of the claim, not examples in an enumeration, and transnational crime is then developed (3.2).
Security Council reform is developed with an effect of its own, better representation and decision-taking for every region (3.2, 4.10).

Albanian territory as a venue for local and international criminal activities is crime with no type named (5.2), and the region's crises and conflicts, identifiable by place, are the subject of a causal sentence (4.10).
An increase in gangs and violent criminal activities pairs gangs with crime in general as the object of the sentence, which counts for both (5.2).
Progress against drug cartels and narco-barons is made the condition for defeating the terrorist underground, a crime-terror nexus with the organizations as its object (5.1).
Confiscating illicit drug wealth is a means against one named crime, which the drugs lens covers, not laundering, stolen-asset recovery or a named non-conviction forfeiture (4.5, 5.1).
The murder and torture of African patriots by the 'police Government' is the object of the claim and is police conduct toward opponents, which counts whoever the victims (4.9).
The conflicts are located in Africa and the Middle East and their toll is the claim of a sentence, so the place gives a referent rather than a general invocation (4.10).

Signing the Freetown Commitment on combating drug trafficking adopts a drug-control instrument, while law-enforcement capacity appears only as a cause of vulnerability to organized crime (3.2, 4.1, 4.9).
Terror practised by certain States on our soil, the subject of repeated complaint, is a specific hostile situation against the speaker's territory, as in 'the shelling of our border towns' (4.10).
The trial irregularities and the shooting of the acquitted men by a sheriff and a policeman are courts and police use of force, which count whoever the victims and whatever the polemic (3.3, 4.9).

Upholding international humanitarian law in Afghanistan after its recent developments concerns an identifiable conflict situation, and the Middle East and North Africa are named as a region of strife (4.10).
The fight against corruption is one of three outcomes that the reforms as a whole will ensure, a shared subject that develops no single item (3.2).
Judicial cooperation, high-security prisons and the tribunal are means against the named crimes (drugs, terrorism, organized crime), not the justice system or crime in general (4.9, 5.1).
The cold war is one item of an enumeration of past priorities, and poverty is otherwise framed through peace-and-security formulas with no concrete conflict prevention (3.2, 4.10).

The review conference of the Programme of Action on the illicit small arms trade is the subject of two sentences, not only a name, and the illicit trade is organized_crime whoever receives the arms (3.2, 4.4).
Not paying the smugglers or the coyotes are items in a series of warnings with a shared addressee and reason, with no fact of their own (3.2).

The reason clause is a clause of its own claiming that drug trafficking produces all forms of corruption and is a ubiquitous link in crime, link claims substantive for corruption and crime in general (3.2, 5.2).
Eliminating hotbeds of conflict is presented as a general task of the Organization, with no conflict, situation or specific decision identified (4.10).
Alternative development is an item of a series of requests but is developed as Bolivia's own contribution to the field (3.2).
Abductions listed with harassment and criminal acts by gangs are kidnapping by criminal groups, row (c), not hostage-taking (5.2).
Terrorism and organized crime are the paired object of the claim that this forum is where they can be fought, not examples in an enumeration (3.2).
'Other criminal activities' is crime with no type named, and the sentence claims its alliance with terrorism, substantive for each item linked (3.2, 5.2).
Illicit trade routes from drugs to plutonium are smuggling of goods, and a clause of its own claims their global spread, developed by what the trade does to social environments (3.2, 4.4).
The passage is about organized crime's financing from drug trafficking, drug terrorism and gold smuggling, a link claim substantive for each source (3.2, 5.1).
Declaring the drug epidemic a health emergency treats drug use as a health problem, a public health response (4.2), while the national body is named without content.
The resolution of regional conflicts, in the region of the proposed anti-terrorist pact, is the subject of its own sentence, not a general invocation (4.10).
Torture still used despite the Assembly's ban, and the internment of sane persons in mental institutions, are torture and arbitrary detention, which count whoever the victims (4.9).
Detaining political suspects for successive ninety-day periods beyond the reach of courts and lawyers is arbitrary detention, which counts beyond the release demand (4.9).
In the verbless sentence naming the challenge to democracy, the relative clause on networks that infiltrate institutions, corrupt justice systems and capture economies carries the point (3.2, 5.1).
Two sentences are about torture used by governments against people, which counts whoever the victims (4.9).
Arms smuggling appears only in a participial phrase qualifying drug trafficking, whose claim is its growth into narco-terrorism (3.2).

The khawarij and extremists are described by motives, deceit and recruitment with no violence against people, and the fragment neither calls them terrorist nor names a listed group (4.6); 'crime' is moral.
The clause that drug addiction is an illness and not a crime is a claim of its own stated as a governing principle, a public health framing of drug use (3.2, 4.2).
The sentence deplores the treatment of those held as hostages, a practice it condemns, and its main clause is about such acts in the Congo, not a war between States (5.2 row (a)).
The last sentence has due process governing the campaign against criminality, crime in general and the justice system's procedure, as its claim (4.9, 5.2).
Urging adoption of the Declaration against torture recommended by the Crime Congress and a study of torture are about torture, which counts whoever the victims (4.9).
Terrorism appears only beside drugs in the closing hope, the two presented as great plagues to be eradicated, with no development (3.2).
'Free of drugs and safe from crime' pairs drugs with crime in general as the object of the main claim, which counts for both (3.2, 5.2).
The illicit circulation of small arms in African subregions is the subject of two sentences, organized_crime whoever receives the arms (4.4).

Sanctioning gang financiers is one undeveloped item of the series of means, while strengthening the police and the Haitian justice system is developed with its own effect, sustained security (3.2, 4.9).
Extremism is named together with violence, so it counts as violent extremism, and the item is developed with an effect of its own in the relative clause (3.2, 4.6).
The 1988 study on financial havens and money laundering is cited only as a precedent for a terrorism-financing study, its topic inside a modifier (3.2, 4.5).
The situation in the north of Ireland is a named situation the speaker has raised before the Security Council, a concrete matter rather than a general invocation (4.10).
The Lockerbie question, Libya's compliance with Council resolutions and the suspension of sanctions are the handling of an act on the closed list (4.6).
Terrorist and criminal activities thriving in lawless zones is the risk the relative clause carries, and crime with no type named counts beside the named crime (5.2).
The evacuation of South African troops is one undeveloped item of the demands of resolution 1702, and the UN presence serves the implementation of decolonization resolutions (3.2, 4.10).
The networks move thousands of tons of drugs, a fact of its own for that item, and the rise of narco-terrorism is the stated cause of the armed-conflict declaration (3.2, 5.1).
Cybercrime legislation is one undeveloped step of a series, and IUU fishing is tackled through fisheries bodies, surveillance and patrols with no criminal groups, prosecution or penalties (3.2, 4.8).
The call to implement the Programme of Action against the illicit small arms trade is a measure against that trade, organized_crime whoever receives the arms (4.4).
The clashes between the socialist camp and the free world are the cold war rivalry of blocs, a concrete matter even when recalled as history (4.10).
The closing contrast of peace ideals with 'obsessive preparation for war' is a general statement with no Powers, arms race or measure identified (4.10).
Criminal behaviour by individual UN troops, and accountability and sanctions for it, is literal crime with no type named, not invective against an army (5.2).
The 1948 violence appears only in a relative clause identifying the writer, and the problem of Palestine only frames a point about wording (3.2).
Transborder trafficking in small arms is organized_crime whoever receives them but is one undeveloped item of a series of measures (3.2, 4.4).
'Economic crimes' names economic crime as one item beside atrocity crimes in the sanctions call, and the financial institutions appear only in a list of actors to involve (3.2, 4.5).
Production options where drug crops are planted and educating and rehabilitating consumers are items of one series of measures, each naming only its target, as in example P3 of 4.2 (3.2).
The National Police appear only in an adjunct crediting them for the country's stability, and 'insecurity' and 'secure' are too vague for criminal_justice (3.2).
The clandestine extremist underground financed by drug profits is neither called terrorist nor tied to violence against people (4.6).
Attacks on embassies and diplomatic representatives, condoned rather than committed by governments, count by their kind as acts against internationally protected persons (4.6).
The first crisis is set amid 'the most intense geopolitical tensions since the Cold War', tension between rival Powers developed with a measure of its own (3.2, 4.10).
The Programme of Action against the illicit small arms trade, whose review conference failed and whose implementation lags, is the object of the claims, not only a name (3.2, 4.4).
'Violence and crime' as the subject of a sentence is crime with no type named, which 5.2 counts even beside terrorism.
The Conference on the Illicit Trade in Small Arms, its agreed conclusions and the assessment of its results are the subject of two sentences, not only a name (3.2, 4.4).
The sentence condemning Munich, whose peace paved the way for the Second World War, is a claim about a specific settlement and war, not only an aspiration (4.10).
Military interference by outside forces in the speaker's own country, blamed for its crisis at the end of last year, is a hostile situation identifiable by place and act (4.10).
The transnational empires of drugs, whose finances are to be attacked, are the object of the claim that they are the root of violence and terrorism (5.1).
Iran's designation as a State sponsor is a national listing, and the militias it trains and arms are not called terrorist, so terrorism itself is not discussed (4.6).
The criminal networks appear only in a participial phrase identifying the terrorist groups, as in B07, so the lens rests on 'transnational crime' and piracy in enumerations (3.2).
